relationships.subject: ethanol
relationships.evidence_quote: ethanol evoked a dose-related, delayed and sustained PMA (~ 6 h)

relationships.subject: acetaldehyde
relationships.evidence_quote: ACD, by targeting TRPA1, releases CGRP from trigeminal nerve terminals that activate CLR/RAMP1 on Schwann cells.

relationships.subject: olcegepant
relationships.evidence_quote: Notably, PMA evoked by ethanol (i.g.) or ACD (i.p.) was prevented by pretreatment with the CGRP receptor antagonist, olcegepant (Fig. 3a, b).

relationships.subject: CGRP receptor (CLR/RAMP1)
relationships.evidence_quote: PMA evoked by ethanol (i.g.) or ACD (i.p.) was markedly attenuated in mice with Schwann cell selective silencing of the RAMP1 subunit of the CGRP receptor

relationships.subject: TRPA1
relationships.evidence_quote: PMA evoked by both ethanol (i.g.) and ACD (i.p.) was prevented in mice with selective silencing of TRPA1 (Plp-CreERT+;Trpa1fl/fl) in Schwann cells (Fig. 4a,b).

key_findings: Ethanol-evoked periorbital allodynia is mediated by acetaldehyde, TRPA1-dependent CGRP release and Schwann cell CGRP receptor signaling, and is independent of TRPV1.
